name: Sprites
description: A Sprite is a hardware-isolated execution environment for arbitrary code: a persistent Linux computer. When working with Claude on your next great idea, Sprites are the simplest answer for "where should I run a blob of code". This MCP server gives you full access to create and manage all of your sprites in a safe way.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Sprites to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Sprites to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://sprites.dev/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Sprites MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sprites lists 18 MCP tools, including checkpoint_create, checkpoint_get, checkpoint_list, checkpoint_restore, create_sprite, destroy_sprite, exec, exec_kill, exec_list, list_sprites, policy_network_get, and policy_network_update.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Sprites?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 18, 2026, alternatives to Sprites in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
Sprites requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Sprites is developed by Fly.io. It is listed as partner on the Claude connector directory.
